newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: TRI to provide ORBCOMM satellite service.
newsitem.headline: TRI to provide ORBCOMM satellite service.

text.p: Malaysia's Technology Resources Industries Bhd (TRI) has signed a licensing agreement with U.S.-based ORBCOMM Global LP to provide satellite services in Singapore, Malaysia and Brunei, ORBCOMM said on Monday.
Azhar Asmuni, vice president ventures of TRI told a press briefing that the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite service will be operational from 1998.
TRI will invest US$7-8 million on building an earth station in Malaysia, marketing and other operational costs, he said.
TRI has already committed US$45 million in equity investment into ORBCOMM's satellite system, Azhar added.
ORBCOMM is a partnership between Orbital Sciences Corporation and Teleglobe Inc of Canada. TRI has a 30 percent stake in Teleglobe.

The ORBCOMM system was launched in 1995 with two operational satellites. Another 34 satellites are being constructed, with 26 scheduled for launch in 1997, said ORBCOMM president and chief executive officer Alan Parker. The other eight satellites will serve initially as spare ground satellites.

ORBCOMM has invested US$260 million in the system out of a total financing resource of US$330 million, said Parker. Of the US$330 million, US$170 million came from a debt offering and the rest from the equity investments of Orbital Sciences, Teleglobe and TRI.

ORBCOMM services provided by TRI will include person-to-person emergency communications, remote industrial assets and environmental monitoring, truck tracking and two way electronic mail in laptop and palm computers.
ORBCOMM services are currently only for data and messaging communictaion.
Parker said ORBCOMM was in negotiations for more licensing deals outside North America. TRI is its second licensee outside North America, the first being in Canada.
